  • Own components of our ML systems, making independent technical trade-offs and keeping them observable, reliable, and well documented
  • Collaborate with a multi-functional agile team spanning user research, design, data science, product management, and engineering to build new product features that advance our mission to connect artists and fans in personalised and relevant ways
  • Prototype new approaches and productionise solutions at scale for our hundreds of millions of active users
  • Help drive optimisation, testing, and tooling to improve quality
  • Unblock and share context with your teammates to raise the whole squad's velocity
  • Use AI-assisted engineering to move faster and remove repetitive toil, while owning the quality of everything you ship
  • Partner closely with senior and staff ML engineers, and be part of an active group of machine learning practitioners in your mission and across Spotify

Working closely with teams across the mission, we develop ML solutions that improve key business metrics, including subscriber growth, monthly active users, and Premium retention.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for someone who can set strategy, lead integrated campaigns, create scroll-stopping social content, and make Spotify one of the most talked-about brands in one of Asia's most vibrant music markets.

    Taiwan is the birthplace of Mandopop and a cultural tastemaker for the broader Chinese-speaking world.     Reporting to the SEA Head of Marketing, you'll work closely with cross-functional teams across Taiwan and the wider region to shape strategy, deliver impactful campaigns, and represent the Taiwan market at a regional and global level.

    You'll partner with teams across Music, Growth, Communications, Business Development, Partnerships, and other functions to bring Spotify's brand to life in Taiwan and help unlock new opportunities for growth.

    • Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We’ll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.
    • Choice in participation: We recognize there’s a wide range of views on the use of generative music tools within the artistic community.     • Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for the use of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.
    • Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will leverage our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    Learn more in our press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:
  • Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users.
  • Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences.
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges.
  • Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization.
  • Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.

We will leverage our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:
  • Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users.
  • Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences.
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges.
  • Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization.
  • Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field. Previous industry experience is helpful.
  • You have experience in one or more of the following fields: generative modeling, machine learning, music information retrieval, speech processing, audio processing, signal processing, probabilistic modeling, computer vision, or related areas.
  • You have deep expertise in at least one of the focus areas above—whether that's vocal/speech synthesis, post-training alignment techniques (e.g., PPO, GRPO, DPO), or audio-to-audio generation and text-guided music editing.
  • You have publications at leading conferences such as ICASSP, ISMIR, INTERSPEECH, ICLR, AAAI, IJCAI, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, or related venues.
  • You have strong coding skills in Python, PyTorch, and NumPy.
  • You are a creative problem solver who is passionate about building outstanding products that add real value to millions of people.
  • You are enthusiastic about turning research ideas into products operating at scale.
  • You can explain complex topics in simple terms, and you enjoy building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders.

    Our Marketing team plays a key role in shaping how people discover, experience and stay connected to Spotify.     ","id":"9057bb9b-3aa2-49ba-9fd0-a9395018d0ea","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

  • Lead Spotify India's consumer retention and engagement marketing strategy across the listener lifecycle, from new and active users to dormant and lapsed listeners.

  • Identify the key drivers of disengagement and churn, and develop targeted strategies that encourage repeat listening and long-term retention.

  • Build tailored retention and re-engagement strategies for different listener segments, using behavioural insights, preferences and engagement patterns.

  • Create personalised listener journeys that connect audiences with relevant music, artists, content and Spotify features.

  • Partner with Data Science, Analytics and Consumer Insights teams to uncover engagement opportunities and turn consumer insights into actionable marketing initiatives.

  • Define and track key performance indicators, including retention, churn, reactivation, daily and monthly active users, and engagement. Use experimentation to measure incremental impact and continuously improve results.

  • Collaborate with Product, Music, Brand, Media and Consumer Marketing teams to develop a connected retention roadmap that brings together product experiences, music releases, artists and cultural moments.

  • Translate insights and performance trends into clear recommendations that influence marketing priorities and drive measurable business outcomes.

    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

  • You understand consumer behaviour and know how to turn insights into strategies that encourage repeat usage and build long-term relationships.

  • You have experience developing segmentation strategies, personalised consumer journeys and engagement programmes for large consumer audiences.

  • You are confident working with data, analytics and experimentation to identify opportunities, evaluate performance and make informed decisions.

  • You think beyond individual campaigns and channels, focusing on how marketing can influence consumer behaviour and deliver measurable business impact.

  • You can bring teams together around shared goals and collaborate effectively with Product, Analytics, Data Science and Marketing partners.

  • You are comfortable balancing long-term strategy with hands-on execution, adapting your approach as you learn what works.

  • You are curious about music, culture and how digital experiences can create meaningful connections with listeners.

    As Revenue Operations Manager, you'll own revenue operations for Spotify Technology, helping our sales organization scale from early growth to a mature, segmented go-to-market model. This is a hands-on role where you'll work closely with the business day to day, identify challenges early, and build the systems, processes, and insights that enable sustainable growth.

    You'll partner with Sales leadership, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success to improve how we operate across the customer lifecycle. You'll balance strategic planning with practical execution, creating structure that helps our teams work efficiently as the business evolves.

    ","id":"66184cac-4d6c-46f6-868c-bac0c184fd22","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Own sales operations for Spotify Technology, including CRM, pipeline management, forecasting, territory and account assignment, and deal desk processes.

    • Design and roll out a segmented sales model that evolves our go-to-market approach as the business matures.

    • Build infrastructure and systems to support a scalable Commercial sales motion (companies with fewer than 1,000 employees), focused on faster deal cycles, efficient lead routing, and repeatable processes.

    • Build infrastructure and systems to support a strategic Enterprise sales motion (companies with 1,000+ employees), enabling prospecting, account planning, and multi-product engagements.

    • Partner with the Director of Sales as a strategic advisor on quota setting, capacity planning, compensation, territory design, and headcount modeling.

    • Support revenue across the full customer lifecycle, including new business, expansion, and retention.

    • Build reporting and dashboards to track pipeline coverage, conversion rates, time to close, forecast accuracy, and net revenue retention by segment.

    • Strengthen forecasting discipline and maintain a healthy, predictable pipeline through effective reporting and sales processes.

    • Identify friction across the sales process, including handoffs between Account Executives, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success, and drive improvements with cross-functional partners.

    • Partner with Marketing on pipeline generation reporting, lead management, and process improvements.

    • Establish and continuously improve operating rhythms, including forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs), as the business scales.

    • Evaluate and manage the go-to-market (GTM) technology stack to support efficient and scalable sales operations.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 6+ years of experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or go-to-market strategy, with a track record of meaningful impact at a senior level.

    • You have experience scaling sales operations through a startup or high-growth phase and understand when to introduce new processes and structure.

Within Platform, our Product Security team evaluates and communicates Spotify's security posture, helping developers and leadership make informed decisions about security risks. We own the vulnerability management platform, supporting the full lifecycle of identifying, attributing, remediating, and reporting security vulnerabilities.

    As AI changes how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited, we're evolving how Spotify responds. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help transform vulnerability findings into reliable, actionable code improvements using agentic AI. You'll build the tools, workflows, and evaluation frameworks that make automated remediation more effective, scalable, and safe, while helping developers focus on building great experiences for our users.

  • Develop tools and processes to compare remediation approaches, evaluate AI models, and continuously improve the reliability and effectiveness of generated fixes.

  • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.

  • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.

  • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.

  • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

    The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

    We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:

    Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.

    Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.

    Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.

    Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    ","id":"babebec3-0061-4c39-a4ad-c51a54d23567","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music.
  • Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms.
  • Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction.
  • Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations.
  • Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust.
  • Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify.
  • Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact.
  • Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are ","content":"
  • You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners.
  • You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior.
  • You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry.
  • You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact.
  • You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities.
  • You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy.
  • You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis.
  • You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces.

    We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work.

    You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale.     ","id":"9d1c90b5-a8a4-4218-b2f3-7bbaefae7fd1","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation.
  • Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions.
  • Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles.
  • Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences.
  • Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify.
  • Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms.
  • Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging.
  • Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data.
  • Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change.
  • Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have 5+ years of professional instructional design experience and a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful work across multiple learning formats.
  • You apply learning science principles such as cognitive load, retrieval practice, spaced learning, and adult learning theory to practical design decisions.
  • You know how to uncover learning and performance needs, translate them into measurable objectives, and design learning journeys that build knowledge and skills over time.
  • You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content.
  • You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate.
  • You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent.
  • You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences.
  • You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes.
  • You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners.
  • You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience.
  • You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI.
  • You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

","description":"

    Spotify is shaping the future of advertising by connecting brands with fans through audio, video, and experiences that are part of people's everyday lives. As our advertising business grows, we're focused on bringing innovative products to market, helping advertisers succeed, and turning new ideas into meaningful business growth.

    We're looking for a Senior Director, Global Advertising Product Marketing to lead the next chapter of our global Advertising Product Marketing team. Reporting to the Head of Advertising Business Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to shape product strategy, strengthen our market position, and help advertisers get more value from Spotify.

    This is an opportunity to build and lead a product marketing function with a clear voice in product decisions and a direct impact on business growth. You'll bring customer insights into product development, establish a disciplined approach to go-to-market execution and product adoption, create compelling reasons for advertisers to choose Spotify, and help a global team deliver measurable results.

    ","id":"b9533f31-7bff-43f6-aaf0-60003f017d88","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for global Advertising Product Marketing, connecting advertiser needs, product innovation, competitive insights, and business growth.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to bring customer and market insights into product decisions and turn innovation into solutions advertisers value.
  • Lead global go-to-market strategies for Spotify's advertising products, including brand and performance advertising, self-service, programmatic, and emerging solutions. Own product positioning, messaging, packaging, launches, and adoption.
  • Build a deeper understanding of advertisers, agencies, buying behaviors, and the competitive landscape. Use these insights to identify opportunities, influence product priorities, and strengthen Spotify's position in the market.
  • Drive product adoption and commercial growth by identifying customer needs, addressing barriers to adoption, and partnering with teams to improve product usage, retention, and revenue. Define clear measures of success and use results to guide future decisions.

    We are looking for an experienced Senior Editor for Indonesia, to join Spotify’s Music Editorial team based in Jakarta. In this role you will be part of the Music team in Southeast Asia, reporting to the regional Head of Editorial.

    You will contribute your expertise to various music-related projects within the company, including playlist curation, creative editorial work, and cross-functional collaboration with different teams in the region and beyond. You will provide deep cultural and musical insights to create highly engaging and cohesive music experiences for listeners, extending beyond playlists, while ensuring an unbiased editorial voice for a wide array of moods, moments, and genres. Additionally, you will drive artist discovery through an extensive editorial ecosystem of playlists and tools, critically assessing music trends and user behavior to identify opportunities and emerging trends.

    You will demonstrate a team player spirit, a passion for performance-oriented analytics, and a solid understanding of Spotify’s role in the music industry both locally and globally. Additionally, you will have an editorial personality that thrives in engaging audiences through creative formats, bringing the playlists to life in innovative ways.

    You will be encouraged to make data-informed decisions while also contributing creative and cultural expertise. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences music and strengthen Spotify’s role as a trusted, culturally relevant voice in the music landscape!

    Spotify's mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.

    The Subscriptions Mission builds and evolves Spotify's subscription products and marketplace experiences to drive sustainable user and revenue growth globally. We focus on awareness, acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization strategies that help users unlock the full value of Spotify while enabling the business to scale efficiently and responsibly.

    This role focuses on the awareness, acquisition, and activation layers of the Subscriptions Mission, making Premium feel unmissable to free users long before a purchase decision. You'll own the strategy for how users discover, understand, and develop intent for Premium value, partnering closely with product, design, engineering, research, marketing, and data science to shape the moments, surfaces, and experiences that drive consideration across markets and segments.

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for Premium awareness, acquisition, and activation, helping more listeners discover its value and take the next step toward subscribing.

  • Own the quality bar for Spotify’s AI voice models, defining what “good enough” means for different products, audiences, languages and use cases.
  • Independently design evaluation rubrics and build an evaluation approach that measures qualities such as naturalness, tone, pacing, pronunciation, accent, audio quality and overall experience.
  • Plan and carry out evaluation campaigns, turning qualitative and quantitative findings into clear recommendations for Voice Production, Speak and product teams.
  • Establish an ongoing evaluation rhythm, including when and how we reassess model quality as our technology and products evolve.
  • Benchmark Spotify’s AI voices against third-party models and competitors to understand where our experiences lead, where they differ and where there are opportunities to improve.
  • Help determine appropriate quality trade-offs as Spotify expands into additional languages and regions, considering the product use case and needs of each market.
  • Partner closely with voice experts, machine learning teams, product partners and vendors to maintain a consistent quality bar across demanding and sometimes competing priorities.
  • Surface the most meaningful gaps in model performance and use evaluation insights to help influence future research and technical priorities.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Spotify is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Authorization team within Platform. Our team builds and operates the authorization and permissioning systems that enable creators and their teams to securely access and manage their presence across Spotify. What began by supporting Spotify for Artists has grown into foundational capabilities used across Spotify, including Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks.

    This is a backend-focused role working on systems that sit on a critical path for Spotify's creator ecosystem. You'll help us evolve these systems as they grow in scale and complexity, bringing strong backend engineering expertise while collaborating across product, frontend, and data when needed.

    ","id":"e04833c0-9cff-4b5e-b217-91a3bcb57051","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do:","content":"

  • Design, build, deploy, and operate scalable backend services that power authorization, permissions, and team management across Spotify.

  • Take ownership of critical systems that enable creators, teams, agents, licensors, and other partners to securely access and manage the right content and capabilities.

  • Evolve our backend architecture to support continued growth in users, use cases, and Spotify products while maintaining high standards for reliability, performance, and security.

  • Improve the systems and workflows that enable creators to gain access to their content, profiles, and teams.

  • Make thoughtful technical decisions and trade-offs, balancing long-term architecture with solutions that meet current product and business needs.

  • Partner with engineers and cross-functional collaborators across Spotify to understand authorization needs and build reusable platform capabilities.

  • Contribute to frontend experiences and data-related work when useful, while bringing deep expertise and leadership to backend engineering.

  • Raise engineering quality through strong technical judgment, design discussions, operational excellence, and knowledge sharing across the team.

    The Content Platform team powers the full lifecycle of content across music, podcasts, audiobooks, and emerging formats at Spotify. We ensure that everything from licensed catalog to user-generated content is understood, trusted, safe, and high quality for millions of listeners worldwide. Our systems are responsible for how content is ingested, understood, enriched, governed, and distributed across the platform.

    As the scale and diversity of content continue to grow—driven by advances in AI, new creation tools, and emerging content formats—we’re investing in intelligent systems that can understand, evaluate, manage, and route content reliably at global scale.

    We’re hiring Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineers to build and scale foundational ML systems that power content understanding, safety, policy enforcement, and decisioning across Spotify. Depending on your experience and interests, you may focus on areas ranging from multimodal content understanding and platform-level ML systems to safety, risk detection, policy enforcement, and compliance.

This work is foundational to delivering safe, high-quality experiences for listeners and creators while enabling new ways for people to interact with content across Spotify.

  • Define the technical direction for policy enforcement infrastructure 

  • Architect enforcement capabilities as a shared platform designed to be consumed by multiple product teams rather

  • Design and evolve multi-signal orchestration systems that enable configurable, auditable policy enforcement at scale across content types and product surfaces

  • Build the data foundation that makes enforcement decisions durable and reusable

  • Own the hardest API and contract decisions: schema design, versioning strategy, and how enforcement interfaces evolve without breaking the teams that depend on them

  • Establish integration standards for teams onboarding onto shared enforcement infrastructure, and work directly with consuming teams to execute migrations with clean cutoffs and clear end states

  • Influence architecture across detection, signal processing, and enforcement workflows so that the underlying primitives stay coherent as the platform scales

  • Mentor engineers and set the bar for how the team reasons about API design, data modeling, and the downstream compliance consequences of infrastructure choices

  • Deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, APIs, event-driven pipelines, rule engines, and decision systems running in production across high-throughput environments

  • Proficient in backend engineering at scale, with strong command of languages like Java, Kotlin, Go, or similar; comfortable owning data models, service contracts, and storage layer decisions

  • Experienced with stream processing and event-driven architectures  (Kafka, Pub/Sub, or equivalent) and the tradeoffs between batch and real-time enforcement pipelines

  • You have designed systems where schema and contract stability matter as much as correctness 

  • Experienced with workflow orchestration and distributed coordination, whether through dedicated orchestration frameworks like Temporal or Airflow, choreography-based event systems, or hybrid approaches, and understand the tradeoffs between each in the context of long-running, stateful enforcement workflows

  • Experienced with relational and non-relational storage systems and know how to model enforcement data for auditability, immutability, and efficient querying at scale

  • You understand platform engineering patterns: multi-tenant APIs, configurable rule engines, policy-driven actioning systems, and the difference between building for one team and building for many

  • Familiar with observability and operational excellence, distributed tracing, structured logging, alerting, and the tooling that makes enforcement systems debuggable and auditable in production

  • You have worked in regulated or compliance-adjacent environments and understand how infrastructure design decisions, log retention, schema choices, data lineage, carry legal and audit consequences

  • You are comfortable in polyglot environments and can navigate existing systems thoughtfully rather than defaulting to greenfield rewrites

  • Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches.
  • Partner closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Data Scientists, and Designers to define and execute experimentation strategies.
  • Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency.
  • Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale.
  • Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of our personalization systems.
  • Mentor and support other Machine Learning Engineers, sharing knowledge and helping strengthen engineering practices across the team.

Tech.eu https://tech.eu en Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:23:24 +0000 hourly 1 <![CDATA[Startups respond to Britain's budget, Greentech Alliance acquires Intermobility, and Europe’s biggest seed rounds of Q3]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/#comments This week, we tracked more than 60 tech funding deals worth over €1.3 billion and over 10 exits, M&A transactions, rumours, and related news stories across Europe.

Britain has no shortage of startup ambition, but can it turn that success into companies that scale and stay? This week's UK Budget introduced Founders' Relief and a raft of measures supporting entrepreneurs, including expanded employee share options, initiatives for female founders and further investment in AI. It's a welcome signal, but tax incentives alone won't solve Britain's scaleup problem.

The UK attracted €14 billion in startup funding in H1 2026, yet access to later-stage capital, customers, talent and infrastructure remains a challenge.

In my follow-up feature, I spoke to founders and ecosystem leaders about what needs to change, from closing regional and gender funding gaps to helping companies commercialise and compete globally. The real test isn't how many startups Britain creates, but how many it can help grow into lasting global businesses.

Want to stay in the know? If email is more your thing, you can always subscribe to our newsletter and receive a more robust version of this round-up delivered to your inbox.

❗ Want to explore the data in more detail? The free, open-access Tech.eu Funding Explorer offers deeper insights into funding rounds, investor activity, company profiles and market trends.

Either way, let's get you up to speed.

🇬🇧 NexGen Cloud closes $106M senior secured term loan facility

🇨🇭 Perceptive Advisors is providing Swiss MedTech company Distalmotion with a loan of up to $70M

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/ Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:23:24 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Beyond the lab: eight European healthtech scaleups taking on medicine’s biggest challenges]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/beyond-the-lab-eight-european-healthtech-scaleups-taking-on-medicines-biggest-challenges/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/beyond-the-lab-eight-european-healthtech-scaleups-taking-on-medicines-biggest-challenges/#comments European healthtech scaleups are tackling some of the industry’s most persistent challenges, from delayed diagnoses and overburdened hospitals to complex diseases with limited effective treatments.  

While their technologies and business models differ, they face a common challenge: translating scientific and engineering breakthroughs into clinically validated, commercially viable products that can reach patients across Europe and beyond, while navigating regulatory approval, healthcare system access and the substantial capital required to scale.

Here are some companies across a variety of verticals to have on your radar:

Diagnostics, AI and patient monitoring

Earlier diagnosis, more accurate assessments and continuous patient monitoring are critical against ageing populations, growing demand and shortages of medical professionals. However, their adoption requires demonstrable clinical value, clinical integration and the necessary regulatory approval and reimbursement.

Checkpoint Care (Bulgaria) 

Check Point Care develops remote patient monitoring tech. Its platform combines wearable medical devices, continuous physiological monitoring and AI-powered clinical decision support. It aims to reduce preventable deaths, hospital readmissions and pressure on healthcare systems by enabling earlier detection and intervention.

The company's wearable devices continuously collect clinical-grade data, including ECG, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate and body temperature.  This information is transmitted to a centralised digital platform, where AI algorithms analyse physiological patterns and generate digital biomarkers.

The system also creates personalised digital twins representing patients' physiological conditions, helping clinicians identify abnormalities and monitor changes over time.

A 24/7 Virtual Care Centre enables clinical teams to analyse patient data and communicate findings to treating physicians.

Ligence develops AI-powered software that automates the analysis of cardiac ultrasound images, helping cardiologists assess heart function and identify potential abnormalities. Its flagship product, Ligence Heart, uses machine learning to analyse echocardiograms, automatically identify anatomical structures, perform measurements and generate structured reports.

Endometrial cancer is one of the most common gynaecological cancers, yet diagnosis can involve invasive procedures, including endometrial biopsies and hysteroscopy. More accessible testing could reduce unnecessary invasive procedures while supporting earlier identification of disease.

Medical devices and interventional technologies

Medical device innovation is transforming how clinicians treat serious conditions, particularly where conventional interventions are invasive, carry significant risks or have limited effectiveness.

Barcelona-based Anaconda Biomed develops medical devices to treat acute ischaemic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot blocks an artery supplying the brain. Its technology focuses on mechanical thrombectomy, a minimally invasive procedure in which physicians use catheters to remove clots and restore blood flow.

The company's ANA Funnel Catheter features a self-expanding, funnel-shaped design intended to improve clot capture, restrict blood flow during retrieval and reduce the risk of clot fragments travelling into smaller vessels. Speed and effectiveness are critical in stroke treatment, as delays in restoring blood flow can result in permanent neurological damage, disability or death. 

Anaconda's tech works alongside existing thrombectomy devices, potentially improving the efficiency of clot removal and reducing complications. Its development reflects the growing importance of specialised neurovascular technologies that can improve outcomes in time-critical medical emergencies.

In September 2026, Anaconda Biomed secured $56 million in financing.

CorWave (France)

CorWave is developing implantable heart pumps for patients with advanced heart failure, using technology inspired by the movement of marine animals.  The technology is designed to reproduce more natural, pulsatile blood flow, adapting to the patient's 

Its Left Ventricular Assist System (LVAS) uses a patented wave membrane to propel blood through the device, rather than the rotary mechanisms used in conventional heart pumps. Existing ventricular assist devices can sustain patients for years, but risks such as bleeding, stroke and blood clot formation remain significant concerns.

CorWave aims to address these limitations by preserving the natural pulse and improving the interaction between mechanical circulatory support and the cardiovascular system. 

In May 2025 CoreWave’s LVAS was implanted in a patient for the first time at St Vincent's Hospital in Sydney, Australia. The patient successfully underwent a heart transplant after 84 days of mechanical support, with no device-related serious adverse events recorded at 30 days. 

Biotechnology and advanced therapeutics

Advances by European biotech companies in genomics, precision medicine, immunotherapy and cellular reprogramming are creating opportunities to target the underlying biological mechanisms of disease rather than simply managing symptoms. 

Arctic Therapeutics (Iceland)

Arctic Therapeutics is developing treatments for complex neurological and inflammatory diseases, drawing on genetic research and population-level health data to identify potential therapeutic targets. 

Its approach combines insights from human genetics with drug development to investigate disease mechanisms and identify opportunities for more targeted treatments.

By using genetic insights to understand the biological drivers of disease, Arctic Therapeutics aims to develop treatments that address underlying mechanisms rather than symptoms alone.

The company focuses on rare neurological diseases and forms of dementia. 

In 2025, Arctic Therapeutics raised €26.5 million Series A.

Asgard Therapeutics (Sweden)

Asgard Therapeutics is developing a new approach to cancer immunotherapy based on in vivo cellular reprogramming. 

Rather than relying solely on conventional treatments that directly attack tumours, the company is investigating how to reprogram cancer cells to stimulate the body's immune system, potentially enabling it to recognise and target malignant cells. Its technology aims to convert tumour cells into cells with antigen-presenting properties, allowing them to activate immune responses against cancer.

This approach could potentially address some of the limitations of existing immunotherapies, which do not work for every patient or cancer type.

Christoph Rieche is a careful, measured speaker, so when he says “I will never forget it”, one tends to lock in.

Rewind to 2010ish, and Rieche, then a well-paid thirtysomething Goldman Sachs executive with itchy feet to launch a startup, met with Index Ventures co-founder Neil Rimer.

Rieche says: “Index was at the time already a pretty famous fund. I was in Geneva for business. Neil happened to be based there. I told him 'I can tell you about my world. Why don’t you tell me more about the VC world?' We were sitting in this meeting, and he said 'we just did an investment, but we haven’t announced it yet. It’s in a company called Funding Circle, and they provide lending to small businesses.’”

The revelation appears to have kick-started Rieche, who had been mulling launching his own Funding Circle AKA Iwoca, into action, as soon after Iwoca was born.

Turning the clock back

Tech.eu is sat opposite Rieche, who is German, in Iwoca’s newish, fresh-smelling London offices (all creams, soft furnishings, and overhanging plants), as the 46-year-old winds back the clock to Iwoca’s early days. Back then, he says, fintech wasn’t a thing; Revolut and Monzo weren’t about and the brands of the day were Spotify and LoveFilm while Rieche was a habitué of Meetup.com (now part of Bending Spoons) where he met his co-founder.

Rieche has now been CEO at Iwoca for nearly 15 years, which, he admits, is a long stint steering a startup or scaleup. But could it all be coming to an end?

Iwoca up for sale?

Sky News reported in June this year that Iwoca, which has raised around £70m in equity and is backed by Augmentum and Commerzbank’s CommerzVentures, was up for sale.

It had hired tech investment bank Qatalyst Partners to oversee the auction, with a sale value of over £1bn. 

Rieche says: “We have shareholders that have been with us for 15 years, some of them. Our last financing round was in 2019, so our youngest shareholder is seven years in. They are all VCs. These kinds of people naturally look for liquidity. It’s quite likely that we will find them some liquidity. But it doesn’t have any impact on our strategy.”

Does that mean an outright sale, IPO or secondary share sale? “I don’t know, these conversations happen literally all the time.”

Iwoca’s launch

You might not have heard of it, but Iwoca is one of the UK’s fastest-growing small business lenders, providing funding for tens of thousands of businesses every year.

It launched in 2012, when Rieche and his co-founder, James Dear, a former Deutsche Bank quant trader (who is stepping down this year), spied an opportunity in the ruins of the financial crisis, which saw banks retreat from SME lending.

Rieche says he was enticed by helping underserved SMEs, the overall market opportunity, and disrupting the legacy banks with tech and data. Today, Iwoca (whose name derives from its mission brief: instant working capital, so I-wo-ca), employs over 700 staff, with offices in London, Leeds, Berlin and Frankfurt.

Iwoca’s offering

Iwoca’s flagship product is SME loans, which range from £1,000 to £1,000,000 in the UK and up to €500,000 in Germany. Loan origination leapt from £952m to £1.5bn in 2025, driving up revenues by 56 per cent to £366m in 2025, Iwoca’s latest financial figures show.

Profits, meanwhile, nearly doubled from £59m to £113m in the period. Its jump in revenues comes amid incumbent banks retreating from SME financing, with challengers like Iwoca eating up market share.

Iwoca, which uses open banking to speed up loan applications, likes to trumpet the speed of its loan approval process, which is largely automated (its record is two minutes and three seconds from a standing start for an approval).

Starling deal

Iwoca also offers loans to Monzo, Starling and Tide customers and other businesses through partnership deals.

On its recently announced deal with Starling, Rieche said: “It’s been a long time in the making. I met Anne Boden about this more than 10 years go. I have been doing this for 15 years now. One thing I have learnt is that things take time. You can’t break through everything in a couple of days.”

One of the big trends in fintech in recent years has been the rise in stablecoin technology but Iwoca says it has no plans to leverage the tech in its lending offering.

Amid observers saying that Iwoca had too narrow an offering, it has recently expanded its product portfolio.

Flushed with “excess liquidity” and “more cognitive energy”, Iwoca has launched a credit score product, business credit card, and an M&A platform to help business buy and sell businesses.

Sanctioned shareholder

In Iwoca’s latest financial results, under the regulatory risk category, there is a reference to London-based VC Redline Capital, which is one of Iwoca’s longest-standing shareholder and owns around a 10 per cent stake in Iwoca. Redline was funded by Vladimir Yevtushenkov, a Russian oligarch, whose daughter Tatiana Evtushenkova has served as its CEO.

In 2023, Redline’s investment in Iwoca was placed under an asset freeze due to sanctions imposed by the UK government related to Yevtushenkov, the billionaire founder of Sistema, the Russian telecoms and media conglomerate

This caused “quite a big headache” for Iwoca, Rieche says. Evtushenkova, who stood down as director of Redline in 2023 according to filings, was removed from the UK sanctions list in 2025.

Rieche says: “These are the great experiences you go through when you are building your own company. Very fortunately for us, that person in the end was removed from the sanctions list last year, so we don’t have any sanctioned shareholders anymore. So, it’s a solved problem.”

Will Iwoca carry out future funding soon? Rieche says no, pointing to Iwoca being profitable.

Running a startup

German stereotypes aside, Rieche is initially a reserved interviewee and appears a methodical man (he did nine months “solid” startup and VC research and two work placements before launching Iwoca).

But once he gets going, he speaks fluidly about the ups and downs of his job (“there are times obviously when you are more motivated than others”), why he’s swerving conferences these days, and London losing its lustre as a fintech hub. Typically, Rieche works from 8.30am until around 8pm, with half his time on Iwoca’s UK business, the rest divided up between its German business and new initiatives.

Of late, he has pulled back on overseas work travel, as he has attending conferences.

He said: “There’s too much to do with the team. The ROI on these events, I think is reasonably low. I spend most of my time with the team and significantly less with the external world.”

Outside work, Rieche, who has two children, spends weekend driving his children around, as well as having an interest in London’s cultural scene.

London losing its appeal

On London as a fintech hub, he says, it has “probably got worse” since he started Iwoca, pointing to an increase in tax and pulling back of entrepreneurs’ incentives (the interview takes place the Autumn Budget).

He says: “Wherever I am looking, things got less flexible for businesses.”

That said, London will remain Iwoca’s headquarters and London “is still a phenomenal city and a magnet”.

The future 

Iwoca has hitherto served more than 100,000 SMEs with loans, but its big ambition is to serve one million.

Whether it will get there and remain independent remains to be seen.

What is apparent is that Rieche has retained an entrepreneurial mindset, albeit with a heavier workload in light of his co-founder exiting. Rieche says his role is “constantly changing” with “different challenges”.

He says: “Now we have started these new initiatives; it really does add a completely new chapter for us.”

As Tech.eu reported yesterday, the Budget introduced a new Founders’ Relief, expanded the Enterprise Management Incentive (EMI) scheme and announced new support for young and female entrepreneurs. It also included further commitments around AI investment, talent and scaleup support.

Chancellor John Healey summed up the problem the government is trying to address:

“Britain does not lack great entrepreneurs. Too often, we invent technologies the world wants here in the UK and see the jobs and profits go somewhere else.”

Europe's funding leader still has a scaleup problem

Britain is hardly starved of venture capital by European standards. The UK remains Europe's biggest destination for startup funding, and Tech.eu's H1 report recorded €14 billion in UK startup equity funding across 423 rounds in H1 2026, up 117.5 per cent year-on-year.

But can British companies access enough patient, later-stage capital to remain independent and scale globally from the UK, rather than eventually looking to US investors, buyers or markets?

Sam Goodsell, Partner and Head of Technology Sector at Menzies LLP, sees the tax change as an incentive for entrepreneurs to keep building rather than accept an early exit, but argues that tax incentives alone will not solve Britain's scaleup problem.

“Becoming a global leader still means raising hundreds of millions of pounds to be noticed,” he said, pointing to the gap between the capital available from many UK investors and the sums deployed by Silicon Valley venture funds.

Owen Ensor, co-founder and CEO of cultivated meat startup Meatly, made a similar distinction:

“The new Founders’ Relief is a welcome announcement and a positive signal that Britain wants to reward entrepreneurs who take risks and build successful companies.

But the bigger opportunity is making Britain the best place in the world not just to start a company, but to scale one.”

Female founders welcome support — but barriers remain

The new programme for female founders adds to existing efforts to tackle the gender gap in venture funding, including the government-backed Women Backing Women initiative, which reached a £130 million first close earlier this year.

Laura Ashforth, co-founder and CEO of Lateral, welcomed the Budget's support but argued that encouraging entrepreneurship requires looking beyond investment incentives.

“We desperately need more people to take on the enormous personal and financial risks required to build the businesses that will drive the UK's future growth.

However, you can’t build a genuinely entrepreneurial economy through investment incentives alone.”

As a female founder with two young children, Ashforth highlighted childcare costs and the £100,000 childcare threshold as examples of policies that can discourage people from taking greater financial risks.

“If we want more people to take entrepreneurial risks, we need to stop making the financially rational choice the least ambitious one.”

The government is also working with its Women in Tech Taskforce to develop two voluntary industry standards. The Inclusive Investment Standard aims to improve transparency in venture capital funding decisions, while the Tech Forward Standard will focus on workplace culture, retention and career progression.

According to WeAreTechWomen's 2025 Lovelace Report, between 40,000 and 60,000 women leave the UK technology sector annually, costing the economy an estimated £2 billion to £3.5 billion.

However, the standards have yet to be finalised, and their voluntary nature raises questions about adoption and accountability. Dr Vanessa Vallely OBE, Founder and CEO of WeAreTechWomen, said:

“The real test will be what happens next. We need to ensure these commitments translate into action, that employers and investors are encouraged to participate, and that progress is measured.”

Taking the startup push beyond London

Planned public procurement reforms include a new Innovation Marketplace, launching in spring 2027, to connect innovative businesses with public-sector buyers. As the UK Business Angels Association notes in its Budget analysis, reforms to the Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) and Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme (SEIS) also leave some industry concerns unresolved, including calls to increase the age limit for eligible businesses.

AI puts industrial policy to the test

He contends that without compute, power and domestic customers, Britain risks financing the early stages of AI companies whose eventual economic value is captured elsewhere. From starting companies to keeping them

The UK has already shown it can produce promising startups and attract substantial venture investment. The harder task is ensuring those companies can access the capital, infrastructure and customers they need to become global businesses without leaving Britain.

The real measure of these initiatives will not be how many programmes are launched or how much funding is announced, but how many companies build lasting businesses in the UK.

The app lets shoppers scan a product in the supermarket and instantly see whether it is an ultra-processed food (UPF), along with healthier alternatives.  More than 70 per cent of products on supermarket shelves are ultra-processed.

A growing body of evidence on UPF’s

UPFs are designed to tempt, backed by clever marketing and often on special offer. In November 2025, an international team of researchers published a series in The Lancet linking the growing share of UPFs in diets worldwide to the rise in chronic disease.

Brussels has taken notice. In July, the European Commission asked its scientific advisers how the EU should define ultra-processed food. Their advice is expected in March 2027.

The Commission has also approached FLTRD co-founder Anke Kuik for her expertise.

“The fact that UPFs are now on the European agenda is an important step,” says Kuik. “It shows this isn’t a passing trend, but a problem that calls for a structural response.”

How does the PureScore work?

The PureScore rates products on three components that together determine the score:

Ingredients: the type and amount of added sugars, fats, salt and additives. Refined ingredients stripped of their nutrients also lower the score.

Processing techniques: processes such as heating, hydrogenation and extrusion that alter the natural structure of food. The more intensive the processing, the lower the score.

Organic certification: organic products score higher because they contain fewer pesticide residues. This structure reflects the three main ways UPFs are thought to affect health: loss of nutrients, the addition of harmful substances and a higher risk of overconsumption.

The FLTRD app now covers more than 150,000 products from seven supermarkets, all of which have a PureScore. This independent, science-based score rates a product’s degree of processing based on its ingredients and processing techniques, so people can easily make healthier choices. 

In the Netherlands, more than 35,000 people already use the app on iPhone and Android.

The goal is for 100 million people to use the PureScore to guide their grocery shopping within five years.

“In France, one in three people already uses a similar app. That’s a clear sign people want more insight and guidance,” says Kuik.

“This investment allows us to bring in the people we need to accelerate.

A structural shift in the market 

Victor Straatman, partner at 4impact capital, shared:

“The European debate on ultra-processed food signals a structural shift in the market. As the European Commission explores which policy frameworks are needed, transparency is becoming a commercial priority for the food sector.

Alongside 4impact, several angel investors from the FMCG industry have participated in the round. One of them is Jeroen Lubbers, who now invests in healthy food initiatives after many years in the sector. 

“Consumers have the right to see at a glance what’s really in a product and what healthier alternatives are available.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/fronted-raises-eur17m-to-simplify-global-hiring-and-business-expansion/ Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:00:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/fronted-raises-eur17m-to-simplify-global-hiring-and-business-expansion/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Entourage raises €100M for second fund, targeting AI, robotics and deeptech]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/entourage-raises-eur100m-for-second-fund-targeting-ai-robotics-and-deeptech/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/entourage-raises-eur100m-for-second-fund-targeting-ai-robotics-and-deeptech/#comments European early-stage venture capital firm Entourage has closed its second fund at €100 million, just over two years after launching its first fund in 2024. The fund exceeded its initial €75 million target within two weeks and was subsequently capped at €100 million.

Founded by Pieterjan Bouten, co-founder and former CEO of Showpad, Entourage focuses on investing in early-stage technology companies.

Since its launch in 2024, Entourage has invested in several European technology companies, including cybersecurity startup Aikido Security, which reached unicorn status earlier this year, Conveo, which recently raised a $50 million Series A, and Lexroom, which reached €30 million in annual recurring revenue within 24 months. Entourage was among the earliest investors in all three companies, backing them before they attracted larger international venture capital investors.

When we launched Entourage two years ago, we had a simple ambition: to back the next generation of legendary founders. We wrote the first cheques into companies like Aikido, Conveo and Lexroom. What these founders have achieved in such a short time has only strengthened our conviction in our generalist, founder-first approach. With Fund II, we’re doubling down,

said Pieterjan (PJ) Bouten, Founder and General Partner of Entourage.

With its second fund, Entourage plans to invest in approximately 25 companies at the pre-seed and seed stages across Europe and other markets. Initial investments will range from €1 million to €5 million, with additional capital reserved for follow-on funding rounds.

While its first fund focused primarily on software companies, the new fund will target a broader range of technologies, including artificial intelligence, enterprise software, robotics, physical AI and deeptech.

The next decade will produce some of the most iconic technology companies in history, and it’s time for Europe to rise to the occasion. AI is reinventing software and taking intelligence into the physical world. Entire industries will be rebuilt. We want to back the founders bold enough to lead that transformation,

said Bouten.

In addition to its investment activities, Entourage operates Entourage Studio, a venture-building arm that combines entrepreneurial talent, capital and operational expertise to co-found new companies. Tekst, an AI-powered enterprise process mining and automation company developed through Entourage Studio, recently raised a €10 million Series A.

Alongside the launch of Fund II, Entourage has expanded its investment team, led by partners Pieterjan Bouten, Evert Beeckman and Maarten Mortier. The firm has added three investors, Erwan Gardelle, Sixtine Riescher and Illja Schiller, opened an office in London and established a presence in Paris.

Entourage also follows an investment approach that limits its involvement in portfolio company governance. Despite leading or co-leading most of its funding rounds, the firm rarely takes board seats, favouring a model that gives founders greater independence in managing their businesses.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/entourage-raises-eur100m-for-second-fund-targeting-ai-robotics-and-deeptech/ Thu, 29 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/entourage-raises-eur100m-for-second-fund-targeting-ai-robotics-and-deeptech/feed 0 false <![CDATA[KineDB raises €850K to rebuild database infrastructure as AI reshapes software development]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/kinedb-raises-eur850k-to-rebuild-database-infrastructure-as-ai-reshapes-software-development/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/kinedb-raises-eur850k-to-rebuild-database-infrastructure-as-ai-reshapes-software-development/#comments KineDB, a company developing database technology for cloud infrastructure and offline devices, has raised €850,000 in pre-seed funding. The round was led by Superhero Capital, with participation from NGL Ventures and angel investors, including Cactos CTO Jussi Pyörre and Kristoffer Abell and Jakob Lilholm, co-CEOs of Danish compliance company Formalize.

Founded by Axel Löwenhoff and Allan Zimmermann, KineDB is developing a general-purpose database designed to operate across different environments, from cloud infrastructure to local devices without an internet connection. The company aims to simplify database management for developers by providing a single system that supports both online and offline operations.

As software development becomes increasingly accessible through AI-powered tools, the number of applications being created continues to grow. This has increased demand on underlying infrastructure, particularly for developers who may lack experience in managing complex database systems.

Axel Löwenhoff, co-founder of KineDB, explained how the growing use of AI in software development is changing the requirements for database infrastructure:

The way AI has opened the gates for developers of all levels to experiment and launch new software is a wonderful thing. A consequence, however, is a lot of software where creators haven’t necessarily considered the underlying databases essential to functionality.
With KineDB, we want to remove that as a layer of complication for engineers, by providing a database that works within this new environment.

To simplify database management for developers, KineDB is building a database engine that can operate both locally within an application and across backend infrastructure. Unlike approaches that rely on separate systems for offline and cloud-based data management, its technology uses a single database engine for both environments.

The company is initially focusing on industries where reliable internet connectivity is not always available. For example, workers in underground mining operations could use KineDB to record progress or equipment conditions on mobile devices while offline, with the information synchronised to a central database once connectivity is restored.

Although its initial focus is on offline data management, KineDB plans to broaden the platform's capabilities to support a wider range of software applications.

The new funding will support the company's development and team expansion, with recruitment focused on engineers specialising in databases, storage systems and query engines.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/kinedb-raises-eur850k-to-rebuild-database-infrastructure-as-ai-reshapes-software-development/ Thu, 29 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/kinedb-raises-eur850k-to-rebuild-database-infrastructure-as-ai-reshapes-software-development/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Auriga Partners announces €80M interim closing for its second cybersecurity fund]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/auriga-partners-announces-eur80m-interim-closing-for-its-second-cybersecurity-fund/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/29/auriga-partners-announces-eur80m-interim-closing-for-its-second-cybersecurity-fund/#comments French venture capital firm Auriga Partners has secured €80 million for Auriga Cyber Ventures II, its second fund dedicated to cybersecurity investments. The fund is targeting a final size of €100 million, with a hard cap of €120 million, and will focus on supporting early-stage European cybersecurity startups.

Auriga Cyber Ventures II will invest in companies from pre-seed to Series A, with initial investment tickets ranging from €500,000 to €5 million. The fund will primarily make minority equity investments and plans to reserve approximately half of its capital for follow-on investments in portfolio companies.

The fund aims to support around 30 European startups, focusing on areas such as AI security, identity protection and data security.

Commenting on the need to strengthen Europe's cybersecurity sector, Geoffroy Rosset, Managing Partner at Auriga Partners, said:

Given the economic, industrial and sovereignty challenges posed by cybersecurity, Europe must equip itself to develop global leaders. We have a particularly dynamic pool of talent, technologies and startups, but they need both substantial capital and specialised support to realise their potential.

The fund has already made its first four investments, backing Finovox, which focuses on document fraud prevention, Fleuret, which develops AI-powered automated penetration testing, Mankinds, specialising in AI systems auditing and compliance, and Nextident, which focuses on AI agent security. Auriga is considering additional investments and aims to complete another two to three deals by the end of 2026.

Auriga Cyber Ventures II follows the firm's first €55 million cybersecurity fund, launched in 2022. Over the past five years, Auriga has backed 30 European cybersecurity startups. Since 2022, the firm has evaluated more than 2,000 companies in the sector. Its first fund has 40 per cent exposure to AI-related technologies and 32 per cent to defence applications.

The firm has also invested in companies including Wallix, Vade and Nexthink. According to Auriga, its investments in Vade and Nexthink generated more than €500 million in distributions to investors during 2025–2026.

Beyond funding, Auriga provides startups with access to a network of investors, entrepreneurs and industry experts. William Lecat, Managing Partner at Auriga Partners, emphasised the importance of this support:

In cybersecurity, the ability to provide hands-on support is just as critical as funding.

The firm's network includes founders and executives from cybersecurity companies such as Wallix, Vade, Sentryo and Oodrive. Through this network, Auriga aims to support portfolio companies with industry expertise, business development and international expansion.
